subject: Error in part3  file NA Filename not recognised

messages.author: 977f7f10ff41acec
messages.subject: Error in part3  file NA Filename not recognised
parts:
Hi all,

I hope this message finds you well. I'm currently facing an issue while running GGIR on UK Biobank data in batches. Some of the cwa files are resulting in the following error:


Error in part3 file NA Filename not recognised. Error in {: task 5 failed - "cannot open the connection" Calls: %dopar% -> <Anonymous> Execution halted.

I'm using the latest version of GGIR, and I'm unsure about the appropriate steps to address this error. Any insights or guidance on how to troubleshoot and resolve this issue would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,

Margaret.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in part3  file NA Filename not recognised
parts:
Hi Margaret,

This sounds like GGIR part 3 is trying to process part 2 output data (milestone data) but cannot find them. This could be due to incorrectly specified path or part 2 not producing any output. For example, when forgetting to update the file path after moving data around  on your drives or when re-using R scripts for multiple studies.

So, you may need to break it down in substeps:
  • If you only run GGIR part 1 and 2 does part 2 then produce the expected output?
  • If you isolate a small subsample of files and processing those with do.parallel = FALSE does that work? and how about setting do.parallel = TRUE?

Best regards,

Vincent

Warning messages: 1: In filesummary[vi:(vi + 6)] <- c(file_summary$Dur_imputed, file_summary$Dur_chsum_failed, : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length 2: In filesummary[vi:(vi + 6)] <- c(file_summary$Nblocks_imputed, file_summary$Nblocks_chsum_failed, : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

Your insights and suggestions on these matters would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards, Margaret

messages.author: c0637b27e3cf6030
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in part3 file NA Filename not recognised
parts:
Margaret,

I did some testing and I think I figured out what caused the warning  you reported,

"Warning messages: 1: In filesummary[vi:(vi + 6)] <- c(file_summary$Dur_imputed, file_summary$Dur_chsum_failed, : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length 2: In filesummary[vi:(vi + 6)] <- c(file_summary$Nblocks_imputed, file_summary$Nblocks_chsum_failed, : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length"

I just sent a pull request addressing this issue, so we'll probably have this fixed soon.

As for why some of your files were reported as corrupt / too short in GGIR 3.0-1 but not in GGIR 3.0-2 -- my guess is that these files have some corrupt blocks in them. I'm guessing that when you were upgrading GGIR you also upgraded GGIRread to the latest 0.3.2, which now imputes corrupt Activity cwa blocks. In the past these blocks were identified as corrupt but still processed, potentially leading to unexpected errors. Since now these blocks are imputed, the file overall doesn't need to be treated as corrupt and can instead be processed normally. The corrupt blocks are reported in the data quality log M$QClog, generated in part 1.

-Lena

Margaret,

If you install the development version of GGIR, the warning you reported will go away:

install.packages("remotes') 
library("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

This will eventually be part of GGIR version 3.0-3.

-Lena

Hi Margaret,

This sounds like GGIR part 3 is trying to process part 2 output data (milestone data) but cannot find them. This could be due to incorrectly specified path or part 2 not producing any output. For example, when forgetting to update the file path after moving data around  on your drives or when re-using R scripts for multiple studies.

So, you may need to break it down in substeps:
  • If you only run GGIR part 1 and 2 does part 2 then produce the expected output?
  • If you isolate a small subsample of files and processing those with do.parallel = FALSE does that work? and how about setting do.parallel = TRUE?

Best regards,

Vincent
